sources.entry: geopandas - Python tools for geographic data (GeoSeries/GeoDataFrame) built on pandas.

summary.one_liner: GeoPandas adds geographic data support to pandas, providing GeoSeries and GeoDataFrame types that hold shapely geometries and perform geometric operations.
summary.what_it_does: GeoPandas extends pandas Series and DataFrame with GeoSeries and GeoDataFrame types that work on shapely geometry objects. Geometry operations are cartesian, and a coordinate reference system (CRS) can be stored on objects and set automatically when loading from a file. Objects can be reprojected to new coordinate systems with to_crs(). Some operations such as area return plain pandas Series, while others such as buffer return GeoPandas objects. Data is read through alternate constructors that accept any format recognized by pyogrio, and objects can be plotted using matplotlib. The README's example reads a zipped ESRI shapefile of New York City borough boundaries using geodatasets.
use_cases: computing areas and buffers of polygons
reprojecting geographic data to a new coordinate system
spatial data analysis in pandas workflows
how_to_run: conda install geopandas (recommended, per the README)
notable: GeoSeries and GeoDataFrame are subclasses of pandas Series and DataFrame
Reads any data format recognized by pyogrio
Reprojection with to_crs() and CRS stored on objects
Governed openly and fiscally sponsored by NumFOCUS
Citable software paper in Computers, Environment and Urban Systems
caveats: Geometry operations are cartesian and there is no enforcement of matching coordinate systems for operations
Low-level geospatial dependencies can be hard to install, so conda is recommended
Plotting requires the optional matplotlib dependency
keywords: work with gis data in python
